The test image is a macro/microscopic close-up of a stem showing:
- White/pale plant tissue background
- Dense, upright brownish-gray branching fungal structures (conidiophores)
- A distinct black mass in the upper right (sclerotium or sporangium)

This is clearly fungal sporulation on a stem. The gray-brown velvety spore structures are characteristic of **Gray Mold** (Botrytis). The part is **stem**.

Candidates from stem index: Alternaria, Anthracnose, Bacterial_Canker, Bacterial_Wilt, Gray_Mold, Late_Blight, Rhizopus_Soft_Rots, Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Blight.

Most likely: **Gray_Mold** — the dense gray-brown conidiophores with black stalks match exactly. Let me confirm with one reference image.

The reference confirms Botrytis conidiophores — branching stalks with grape-like conidia clusters. The test image shows the same structures from a stereomicroscope perspective, with the characteristic brownish-gray color of Botrytis sporulation and what appears to be a sclerotium (black mass) in the upper right.
